name: Pelmanism
description: Pelmanism is a simple memory game in which players turn over two cards at a time from a face-down layout to find matching pairs. Also known as Concentration or Memory; in Japan as Shinkei-suijaku. The British name comes from the Pelman Institute (London, 1899).

content.text: Pelmanism is a simple memory game in which players turn over two cards at a time from a face-down layout to find matching pairs. Also known as Concentration or Memory; in Japan as Shinkei-suijaku. The British name comes from the Pelman Institute (London, 1899).

The name Pelmanism comes from Britain: Christopher Louis Pelman founded the Pelman Institute for the Scientific Development of Mind, Memory and Personality in London in 1899. The game is a simple memory pastime also known as Concentration or Memory (English) and Shinkei-suijaku in Japan.

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 2
Partnerships: None

Type: Standard 52-card deck
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included
Standard 52-card deck, table or floor space. Cards are spread face down and must not overlap.
No cards are dealt to hands. All cards are thoroughly shuffled and spread face down on the playing surface in a regular pattern or irregular layout; positions are fixed for the round.

items.text: Match by rank and colour: When using only two cards of each type (e.g. from a standard pack), players may agree that cards match only if they have the same denomination and the same colour (e.g. both red or both black), making matching harder.

Four of each type: Some packs have four identical cards of each type instead of two, so the first card of a new rank has three possible pairings and the start is easier; the game still gets easier as the layout shrinks.
